story: How do I file my consumer complaint on e-Daakhil? The AC I bought for Rs 38,000 on 5 September 2026 is defective and the shop won't refund.

timeline.event: Purchased a defective AC for Rs 38,000
timeline.user_words: The AC I bought for Rs 38,000 on 5 September 2026 is defective

facts.user_goal: File a consumer complaint on e-Daakhil
missing: Name and address of the shop
State and city of the shop

rules.name: consumer_limitation
rules.message: File your consumer complaint before 05 Sep 2028 (667 days left). This counts 2 years from 05 Sep 2026 (your purchase date - counted from the earliest possible day, to be safe). Don't wait for the last date. Sending a letter or calling the helpline does NOT pause this clock.

facts_used.start_basis: purchase date (earliest possible start, to be safe)

rules.label: Last date to file your consumer complaint

rules.name: forum_and_fee
rules.message: You paid Rs 38,000, so the complaint goes to the District Consumer Commission, with no filing fee. You can file in the district where you live or work, online at e-jagriti.gov.in. You don't need a lawyer to file.
rules.label: Where to file

rules.name: free_first_steps
rules.message: Two free steps often work first: (1) a written complaint to the seller's or platform's grievance officer, (2) the National Consumer Helpline: call 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
rules.label: Try these first

answer.summary: You can file a consumer complaint because the AC is defective. The shop refusing to refund is an unfair trade practice. You have time to file before 5 September 2028. You can file online for free.

claims.text: You are a consumer because you bought the AC for personal use and not for resale or a commercial purpose.
A defective product is a 'defect' under the law.
A shop refusing to refund a defective item is an unfair trade practice.
Your complaint must be filed within two years of the purchase date.
Because you paid Rs 38,000, your case goes to the District Commission and there is no filing fee.

next_steps.action: Gather the shop's name and address.
next_steps.why: You need this to file the complaint.

next_steps.action: Find out the exact date the shop refused your refund.
next_steps.why: This date starts your two-year legal clock.

next_steps.action: Call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 or WhatsApp 8800001915.
next_steps.why: This is a free first step that can often resolve the issue without a formal complaint.

next_steps.action: File your complaint online at e-jagriti.gov.in.
next_steps.why: You can file for free in your district without a lawyer.

support.text: You are a consumer because you bought the AC for personal use and not for resale or a commercial purpose.
support.reason: The law text defines 'consumer' to exclude persons who obtain goods for resale or for any commercial purpose. The sentence states the person bought the AC for personal use and not for resale or commercial purpose, which directly aligns with the law's definition.

support.text: A defective product is a 'defect' under the law.
support.reason: The law text defines 'defect' as any fault, imperfection or shortcoming in the quality, quantity, potency, purity or standard required to be maintained by law, contract, or as claimed by the trader. A defective product is therefore covered by this definition.

support.text: A shop refusing to refund a defective item is an unfair trade practice.
support.reason: The law text explicitly lists as an unfair trade practice: 'refusing, after selling goods or rendering services, to take back or withdraw defective goods or to withdraw or discontinue deficient services and to refund the consideration thereof... within the period stipulated in the bill or cash memo or receipt or in the absence of such stipulation, within a period of thirty days.' The sentence describes exactly this scenario.

support.text: Your complaint must be filed within two years of the purchase date.
support.reason: The law text states that the District Commission, State Commission or National Commission shall not admit a complaint unless it is filed within two years from the date on which the cause of action has arisen. This directly supports the sentence.

support.text: Because you paid Rs 38,000, your case goes to the District Commission and there is no filing fee.
support.reason: The law text states District Commission jurisdiction is up to Rs 50 lakh, which is correct for Rs 38,000. However, the law text does not mention anything about 'no filing fee' - it only provides the pecuniary jurisdiction limits. The sentence adds a filing fee condition that is not in the law text.

support.text: Because you paid Rs 38,000, your case goes to the District Commission and there is no filing fee.
support.reason: The law text states 'No fee where the consideration paid is up to Rs 5 lakh.' For Rs 38,000 (which is above Rs 5 lakh), the fee would be Rs 200, not 'no filing fee.' The sentence incorrectly states there is no filing fee.

support.text: Because you paid Rs 38,000, your case goes to the District Commission and there is no filing fee.
support.reason: The law text states District Commission jurisdiction is where value 'does not exceed one crore rupees' (with provision for Central Government to prescribe other values). While Rs 38,000 is within Rs 1 crore, the law text does not mention anything about 'no filing fee.' The sentence adds a filing fee condition not present in the law text.

support.text: Because you paid Rs 38,000, your case goes to the District Commission and there is no filing fee.
support.reason: The law text provides jurisdictional rules for where to institute a complaint (local limits based on opposite party residence, business, branch office, or where cause of action arises, or complainant's residence). It does not mention anything about 'no filing fee' or that the case 'goes to the District Commission' based solely on the amount paid. The sentence adds conditions not in the law text.

draft:
Date: 08 November 2026
From: [FILL: your full name], [FILL: your full postal address]
To: [FILL: name of the other party], [FILL: their address / registered office / email]

Subject: Demand for refund

On 05 September 2026 I paid Rs 38,000 to you for [FILL: product/service and order number]. [FILL: what went wrong, e.g. product defective / service not provided]. Despite my requests you have not refunded the amount.

I request a full refund of Rs 38,000 within 15 days of receiving this letter.

If the refund is not made, I intend to file a complaint before the District Consumer Commission under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, without further notice to you.

I have the following records: [FILL: receipts, chats, emails, bank statements].

Yours faithfully,
[FILL: your name and signature]

draft_notes:
How to send it:
1. Find their correct address in the invoice, order page, or the seller's 'grievance officer' details on the website/app.
2. Fill every [FILL] slot. Remove anything that isn't true - only state facts you can prove.
3. Send by Speed Post and keep the receipt and the tracking proof of delivery. Also send a copy by email or WhatsApp and keep a screenshot.
4. Wait 15 days. Sending this letter does NOT stop any legal time limit - file your claim/complaint before the deadline shown, even if they haven't replied.
5. Free help to check the letter: legal aid 15100 or Tele-Law 14454.

Laws this letter relies on: Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.69 (Two-year limitation and condonation); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.34(2) (Where to file: District Commission); Consumer Protection Act, 2019, s.35(1) (Who may file a complaint; e-filing)
